questions.q: Using the method 'Meaning of Depreciation', work with: cost = 5000, salvage_value = 25, useful_life = 400. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_depreciation.

Take the relation taught for 'Meaning of Depreciation' and work with: cost = 120000, salvage_value = 500, useful_life = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_depreciation.
Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Depreciation' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic and permanent reduction in the book value of a tangible fixed asset due to usage, the passage of time, or technological obsolescence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Depreciation'.
questions.a: Allocation of the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life as an expense.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Meaning of Depreciation', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate annual depreciation using straight line method. Use the method 'Straight Line Method'. Work with: cost = 500, salvage_value = 500, useful_life = 400. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rate.

Find the rate of depreciation under fixed installment method. Use the method 'Straight Line Method'. Work with: cost = 2500, salvage_value = 500, useful_life = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rate.
Explain in your own words what 'Straight Line Method' refers to.
questions.a: A depreciation method where an equal amount is charged as an expense in every accounting period over the asset's useful life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Straight Line Method'.
questions.a: Uniform depreciation charge throughout the asset's life.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Straight Line Method', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate depreciation using written down value method. Use the method 'Written Down Value Method'. Work with: cost = 20000, rate = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of depreciation_2.

Determine the depreciation for the second year using WDV. Use the method 'Written Down Value Method'. Work with: cost = 2500, rate = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of depreciation_2.
Explain in your own words what 'Written Down Value Method' refers to.
questions.a: A depreciation method where a fixed percentage is applied to the book value of the asset at the beginning of each year, resulting in declining depreciation charges.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Written Down Value Method'.
questions.a: Higher depreciation in early years, reducing over time.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Written Down Value Method', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Secret Reserve', work with: actual_net_worth = 30, disclosed_net_worth = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of secret_reserve.
Take the relation taught for 'Secret Reserve' and work with: actual_net_worth = 50, disclosed_net_worth = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of secret_reserve.
Explain in your own words what 'Secret Reserve' refers to.
questions.a: A financial reserve that is intentionally omitted from the balance sheet to understate profits or financial strength.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Secret Reserve'.
questions.a: Created by overstating liabilities or understating assets to provide a buffer for lean periods.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Secret Reserve', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate annual depreciation using straight line method. Use the method 'Depreciation'. Work with: original_cost = 1200, salvage_value = 10, useful_life = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_depreciation.

Find the depreciation amount. Use the method 'Depreciation'. Work with: original_cost = 500, salvage_value = 25, useful_life = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of annual_depreciation.
Explain in your own words what 'Depreciation' refers to.
questions.a: The permanent and gradual shrinkage in the book value of a tangible fixed asset due to usage, time, or obsolescence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Depreciation'.
questions.a: Allocating the cost of a tangible asset over its productive years.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Depreciation', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Depletion and Amortisation', work with: cost = 80000, legal_life = 45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of amortisation_rate.
Take the relation taught for 'Depletion and Amortisation' and work with: cost = 500, legal_life = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of amortisation_rate.
Explain in your own words what 'Depletion and Amortisation' refers to.
questions.a: Depletion refers to the exhaustion of natural resources, while amortisation is the write-off of intangible assets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Depletion and Amortisation'.
questions.a: Specific terms for value reduction based on asset type (natural vs intangible).

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Depletion and Amortisation', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate depreciation using WDV method. Use the method 'Written Down Value Method'. Work with: book_value = 12000, rate = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_book_value.

Find the book value after 3 years using diminishing balance method. Use the method 'Written Down Value Method'. Work with: book_value = 50000, rate = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_book_value.
Explain in your own words what 'Written Down Value Method' refers to.
questions.a: A depreciation technique where a fixed percentage is applied to the book value of the asset at the start of every year.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Written Down Value Method'.
questions.a: Depreciation amount decreases every year as the asset's book value reduces.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Written Down Value Method', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Provisions vs Reserves', work with: gross_profit = 5000, provisions = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_profit.
Take the relation taught for 'Provisions vs Reserves' and work with: gross_profit = 80000, provisions = 45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_profit.
Explain in your own words what 'Provisions vs Reserves' refers to.
questions.a: Provisions are charges against profit for known liabilities of uncertain amounts; reserves are appropriations of profit to strengthen finances.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Provisions vs Reserves'.
questions.a: Provisions are mandatory expenses; reserves are optional earnings retentions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Provisions vs Reserves', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate new provision for doubtful debts. Use the method 'Provision for Doubtful Debts'. Work with: bad_debts = 360, debtors = 300, further_bad_debts = 240, old_provision = 150, rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pl_charge.

Find the amount to be debited to P&L for bad debts. Use the method 'Provision for Doubtful Debts'. Work with: bad_debts = 120, debtors = 120, further_bad_debts = 20, old_provision = 45, rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of pl_charge.
Explain in your own words what 'Provision for Doubtful Debts' refers to.
questions.a: An estimated amount set aside to cover potential losses from debtors who may not pay.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Provision for Doubtful Debts'.
questions.a: Calculated on the net debtors after deducting unrecorded bad debts.
